quoted_clause: Reproduction status is recorded per family in the First-hand Sources list (A.10): each entry carries its source URL/identifier, the version and release date where known, and the verification status (whether the claim is vendor-reported [1P] pending independent check, or independently verified).
observed: The visible A.10 entries do not carry per-family verification status or, in several cases, release dates; they only list sources and a general compiled note.
evidence: A.10 list: DeepSeek entry has no release date or verification status; Kimi entry has no release date or verification status; Qwen entry has no release date or verification status; GLM entry has date but no explicit verification status.
root_cause: Overstated description of the source list.
correction: Either add the claimed fields to each A.10 entry (version/release date where known, verification status) or reword: 'The First-hand Sources list records the source identifiers; the general compiled note states that all parameters/claims are vendor-reported [1P] and require verification on the architect's own hardware.'
acceptance_test: The text's description matches the actual A.10 entries.

quoted_clause: circuit breaker activation reduces tail latency for remaining requests by 35% because the system sheds load before the model queue fills.
observed: The 35% reduction is a specific quantitative effect but is not derived from any stated queueing model; it is labeled [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION], yet the causal 'because' can make it read as a mechanism-level expectation.
evidence: No calculation in the chunk derives 35%; it is a scenario input.
root_cause: Quantified assumption presented with causal language.
correction: Reword as 'In this scenario, assume circuit-breaker activation reduces tail latency for remaining requests by 35%; this is an input to be measured, not a derived effect.' Or remove the percentage until a queueing model supports it.
acceptance_test: The percentage is clearly an assumed scenario input, not a derived or generally expected effect.

quoted_clause: These components sum to a ~450 ms baseline TTFT budget, which the capstone declares as the baseline p99 scenario value (a scenario input, not a derived quantile of a distributed sample; a real baseline p99 must come from a measured latency distribution). The 450 ms is a service-time sum with no queueing term; at the offered ~2 rps against the ~2.0 req/s analytical ceiling (ρ near 1), a real queueing delay sits on top
observed: The text calls 450 ms a 'baseline p99 scenario value' while also stating it is a service-time sum with no queueing term and that at ρ near 1 a real queueing delay sits on top. This can mislead readers into treating a service-time sum as a p99 latency.
evidence: The quoted sentence itself distinguishes service-time sum from measured p99.
root_cause: Terminology overload: 'p99 scenario value' used for an assumed service-time target.
correction: Change to 'baseline service-time target' or 'assumed baseline p99 service-time component' and keep the warning that a real p99 must include queueing.
acceptance_test: The 450 ms is not labeled a p99 unless it is explicitly an assumed p99 service-time component, and the text says real p99 includes queueing.

quoted_clause: it reports 3.0× less attention compute and a 4.4× smaller KV cache
observed: '3.0× less' is nonstandard and can be misread; multiplicative reductions should be phrased as 'lower', 'reduced by a factor of', or 'one-third' if that is the intended meaning.
evidence: The adjacent text says the measures are normalized per-head/per-layer and are not whole-model ratios, so precise wording matters.
root_cause: Awkward multiplicative phrasing.
correction: Use '3.0× lower attention compute' or 'attention compute reduced by a factor of 3.0' (if that is the vendor's intended ratio).
acceptance_test: No '× less' phrasing remains in the GLM comparison.

quoted_clause: Re-verifying the serving-status row on release day reclassifies nothing above it: the August architecture evidence stays exactly as it was compiled. [1P]
observed: The [1P] tag appears after a methodological sentence about the appendix's own register discipline, not after a first-party vendor claim. It may mislabel the sentence as first-party evidence.
evidence: The sentence is about re-verification and snapshot immutability; no vendor source is cited in that clause.
root_cause: Stray or mis-scoped provenance tag.
correction: Remove the [1P] tag from that sentence, or move it to the specific first-party source row if it was intended to tag the table.
acceptance_test: [1P] tags only first-party source claims, not the book's methodological statements.

page_hint: Appendix A, four-family list and §2 Kimi K3
quoted_clause: stable-LatentMoE activating 16 of 896 routed experts
observed: The same mechanism is later named 'Stable LatentMoE' with different capitalization and spacing. This is a minor terminology inconsistency for a named vendor mechanism.
evidence: Four-family list: 'stable-LatentMoE activating 16 of 896 routed experts'; §2: 'Stable LatentMoE activating just 16 of 896 routed experts per token'.
root_cause: Inconsistent naming.
correction: Use the vendor's exact name consistently, likely 'Stable LatentMoE' or 'Stable-LatentMoE' if that is the official spelling.
acceptance_test: The mechanism name is spelled the same way throughout the appendix.

quoted_clause: A typical re-sizing that lets the peak load concentrate on the canonical fleet would have to be computed under §26.8's cost-basis rules — §26.8 states those rules but does not perform the re-sizing — and it is not a 48% figure
observed: The phrase 'lets the peak load concentrate on the canonical fleet' is unclear; re-sizing normally changes fleet size to absorb or distribute load, not to concentrate it. The sentence is hard to parse and may misstate the excluded calculation.
evidence: The surrounding text discusses fixed fleet and re-sizing; no definition of 'concentrate' is given.
root_cause: Awkward compression.
correction: Rewrite as: 'Any re-sizing that would allow the canonical fleet to absorb the peak load at a lower all-in cost would have to be computed under §26.8's cost-basis rules; §26.8 states those rules but does not perform that re-sizing, and it is not a 48% figure.'
acceptance_test: The sentence clearly states what re-sizing is being excluded and why.

issue: The drawn roofline is inconsistent with its labeled ridge (~295) and peak (1e15 FLOP/s): the black memory-bound segment starts at ~1e12 FLOP/s at AI=1 and reaches 1e15 at ~295, which implies bandwidth ~1e12 B/s and ridge ~1000, not ~295. The decode marker at AI~1, ~3e12 FLOP/s therefore sits above the drawn roof.
evidence: Axes: x 'arithmetic intensity (FLOP/byte)' 1..10000; y 'attainable performance (FLOP/s)' 1e11..1e15. Black line starts at (1,1e12), corner at red dashed 'roofline ridge ~295' and flat roof 1e15. Caption: 'decode at ~1 FLOP/byte' and '~295 ridge'. Roofline formula: attainable = min(peak, B*AI); B = peak/ridge = 1e15/295 ≈ 3.39e12 B/s, so at AI=1 the roof is ~3.39e12, not 1e12. The red decode dot is plotted at ~3e12, above the drawn line.
acceptance_test: Recompute B from the stated peak and ridge; redraw the memory-bound segment through (1, B) and (ridge, peak) with slope 1 on log-log axes; place the decode marker on or below the roof (or replace it with a non-quantitative regime label); verify no marker lies above the roof and that the ridge label matches the drawn corner.

issue: The Token IDs box says 'integers order = position', which conflates token identity with positional encoding. Token IDs are vocabulary indices; position IDs are assigned separately and encoded by the model.
evidence: Label in the Token IDs box: 'integers / order = position'. The caption says 'text → tokenizer → IDs → embedding → attention' and does not mention position IDs. A reader can infer that the integer token ID encodes its position.
acceptance_test: Replace the label with 'integers; sequence order preserved' and add a separate 'position IDs' annotation on the path to the transformer/attention, or explicitly state that positions are assigned separately. Verify no arrow or label implies token ID = position.

issue: The arrow from Embedding to Attention is labeled 'attend', and the Attention box says 'computes Q, K, V for this token vs all past tokens'. This conflates the projection that produces Q/K/V with the attention operation and can imply that the embedding itself attends or that K/V for past tokens are recomputed.
evidence: Arrow label 'attend' between 'Embedding' and 'Attention'; Attention box text 'computes Q, K, V for this token vs all past tokens'; KV Cache box says 'read + write per layer × head' and the return arrow is labeled 'read past K,V'.
acceptance_test: Relabel the Embedding→Attention arrow 'project Q/K/V' or 'hidden state'; change the Attention box to 'Q from this token; attend over cached past K/V' (or equivalent). Keep 'attend' only for the attention operation, not the embedding transition.

issue: The diagram visually separates token1 ('sampled by prefill') from token2/3 and routes token1 into the top of 'append K/V', which can imply that prefill writes token1's K/V. The caption says a token's K/V is written when it is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled.
evidence: Token1 box: 'token1 / sampled by prefill'; token2: 'first decode output'; token3: 'second decode output'. All feed 'append K/V per layer-head'. Caption: 'written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled.'
acceptance_test: Add a step boundary or label the token1 path 'appended on first decode' and make the token1/2/3 entry paths visually uniform; verify the figure alone does not imply prefill appends token1's K/V.

issue: Secondary labels are set in small, low-contrast gray type below the 8 pt print floor: 'sampled by prefill', 'first decode output', 'second decode output', 'store K', 'store V', 'read V', 'read K'.
evidence: Rendered page at 150 dpi: these labels are visibly smaller and lighter than the box titles; at print size they are difficult to read, especially in grayscale.
acceptance_test: Increase these labels to at least 8 pt and darken to a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the background; verify at 100% print size and in grayscale.

issue: The 'read' path from the persistent KV cache to the decode transformer is drawn as a plain vertical line without a visible arrowhead, while the 'append' path has a clear upward arrowhead. The direction of the read path is therefore ambiguous.
evidence: Between 'PERSISTENT KV CACHE' and the DECODE transformer: left vertical line labeled 'read' has no visible arrowhead; right vertical line labeled 'append' has an upward arrowhead. Caption: 'each step reads the cached K/V, appends the new K/V'.
acceptance_test: Add a downward arrowhead to the 'read' path and make the read/append pair visually symmetric; verify the direction is unambiguous without relying on the caption.

issue: Several figure annotations are below the 8 pt print floor and low contrast: 'populate', 'read', 'append', 'initialize', 'loop', and 'conceptual per-step, per-layer cache I/O'.
evidence: Rendered page at 150 dpi: these labels are visibly smaller than the box text; 'conceptual per-step, per-layer cache I/O' is especially small and light gray.
acceptance_test: Enlarge all figure annotations to at least 8 pt and darken low-contrast labels; verify at 100% print size and in grayscale.

figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior
issue: The MoE resident-memory components shown in the figure do not visibly sum to the stated total. The figure labels 'inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)' and 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)' and then states 'MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB'. The two visible components sum to about 91 GB; the missing ~3 GB is the always-on/shared resident weight, which is mentioned only in the per-token active-compute line ('1.4B always-on') and in the caption's italic paragraph, not as a resident-memory component.
evidence: Figure 3.4 labels: 'inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)'; 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'; 'MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB'. Arithmetic: 68.4 + 22.8 = 91.2 GB. The caption and italic paragraph identify 'always-on attention/shared weights (~1.4B)', which at FP16 is ~2.8 GB, giving ~94.0 GB total. The figure does not label that resident component, so the displayed decomposition does not close.
acceptance_test: Add an explicit always-on/shared resident component to the MoE legend (e.g. 'always-on/shared ≈ 3 GB') or restate the total as '≈ 91 GB experts + ≈ 3 GB always-on = ≈ 94 GB'. Recompute the displayed components so that they visibly sum to the stated total within rounding.

figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior
issue: The figure uses '11.4' in two different unit contexts without local disambiguation: '2 × 11.4' in the resident-memory legend means 11.4 GB per expert, while '11.4B top-2' in the per-token line means 11.4 billion active expert parameters. The caption resolves this, but the figure itself can be misread as mixing GB and B.
evidence: Legend: 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'. Per-token line: 'per token: 11.4B top-2 + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB'. The first '11.4' is GB per expert; the second '11.4B' is billion parameters for the two active experts. The numbers coincide because 5.7B parameters at FP16 is 11.4 GB per expert, but the unit shift is not marked inside the legend.
acceptance_test: Make the units explicit in both places, e.g. 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4 GB)' and '11.4B active expert params (2 × 5.7B)'. Verify that a reader can distinguish resident bytes from active parameter count without consulting the caption.

figure: Figure 6.1 — The metric hierarchy as a diagnostic chain
issue: The caption claims the figure shows 'the bottom-up diagnostic path from a p95 TTFT breach to its root cause', but the drawn figure shows only the generic three-layer hierarchy and generic upward/downward arrows. No p95 TTFT breach, no specific root cause, and no traced path are drawn. The caption overstates the figure's specificity.
evidence: Figure 6.1 contains three boxes: 'Workload metrics', 'Resource metrics', 'Serving metrics'; a green downward 'causation' arrow; a red dashed upward 'diagnosis' arrow; and the note 'causation ↓ (workload → resource → serving) | diagnosis ↑ (serving → resource → workload)'. Caption: 'The three metric layers and the bottom-up diagnostic path from a p95 TTFT breach to its root cause.' The figure does not label p95 TTFT or a root cause.
acceptance_test: Either add a specific callout path to the figure (e.g. 'p95 TTFT breach' at Serving → 'prefill queueing / KV pressure' at Resource → 'context-length growth' at Workload) or revise the caption to say the figure shows the generic diagnostic direction, with the p95 TTFT example belonging to the surrounding prose.

issue: The diagram labels the baseline inputs as '1 · FACT' and 'baseline TTFT p99 450 ms', but the facing text explicitly says these are assumed inputs, not gathered facts, and that the 450 ms is a service-time sum with no queueing term, not a measured p99 distribution.
evidence: Figure box: '1 · FACT' / 'baseline TTFT p99 450 ms'. Page 410: 'These are assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTs (R-07)' and 'the 450 ms is a service-time sum with no queueing term' and 'the per-query values are not a p99 of a separate measured distribution.'
acceptance_test: Relabel the box to 'ASSUMPTION / BASELINE INPUT' (or equivalent) and change the caption/loop label from 'FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN' to 'ASSUMPTION → DERIVED → PATTERN'; if 'p99' is retained, qualify it as 'scenario p99' or 'assumed p99' and ensure no unmeasured value is labeled FACT.

issue: The 'DERIVED' box states 'decode bandwidth-bound' as a bare property, while the prose says this is a low-batch regime whose persistence depends on batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware.
evidence: Figure box 2: 'decode bandwidth-bound'. Page 410: 'sharding distributes the model across the node so decode lands in the bandwidth-bound regime (the low-batch regime of Ch. 8; batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there)'.
acceptance_test: Add the regime qualifier to the box, e.g. 'decode: bandwidth-bound in this low-batch scenario', or add a caption sentence that the box is a scenario-specific derived regime, not a universal property.

issue: The table places vendor-reported percentages with different metric scopes in the same 'KV cache*' and 'Compute*' columns, inviting cross-row comparison even though the caption/footnote say the scopes differ.
evidence: Table columns 'KV cache*' and 'Compute*'; GLM row has '~23%' with 'BF16 / layer' and '~33%' with 'attention only per head / layer'; footnote says '*Metric scopes differ'; caption says 'GLM's rows are per-layer/per-head scope, not total FLOPs or total cache'.
acceptance_test: Split the columns by scope (e.g. 'Total KV / total compute' vs 'per-layer/per-head attention') or add an explicit 'Scope' column and visually separate GLM's attention-only values from DeepSeek's total-model values; the reader should not be able to compare 10% and 33% as the same metric.

issue: The stacked bars with increasing dates visually encode a chronology/layering that the caption explicitly disclaims ('not a causal lineage', 'a later layer does not require the one below it', 'eras overlap'). The drawing still reads as a sequential stack from Transformer to Agent Fleet.
evidence: Figure: stacked bars 'Transformer ~2017' through 'Agent Fleet ~2026'. Caption: 'the vertical stacking is a layering ... not a causal lineage: a later layer does not require the one below it, and the eras overlap.'
acceptance_test: Redraw as a timeline with overlapping era bands, or as a non-stacked set of era markers; if the stack is retained, add an explicit visual break/annotation that the vertical order is not dependency or chronology, and remove the date column's implication of a single sequence.

issue: The color legend 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs' misclassifies 'Inside post-training' (and arguably 'Inside test-time search') as system-side, although post-training is a model-development/training activity and test-time search can be model-inference compute.

acceptance_test: Recolor 'Inside post-training' as model-side or replace the binary legend with a three-way or explicit placement taxonomy (model internals / model development / system orchestration); ensure every band's color matches its stated definition.

issue: In the 'Actual stop' path, a solid flow arrow runs from pass 2 into the dashed 'pass 3 not executed' box, while the actual exit is a separate orange arrow from pass 2 to exit. The mixed solid-arrow-into-dashed-box encoding makes the reading order ambiguous.

issue: The p50, p90, and p95 reference lines are all rendered in the same green dashed style and are packed within a narrow band (~0.80–0.99 s). At print size the three lines are distinguishable mainly by their small stacked labels, not by visual encoding.

acceptance_test: Either give p50/p90/p95 distinct line styles or markers, or add a small inset/legend that maps each percentile to its line without relying on color alone; verify the figure remains readable in grayscale at 100% print size.

issue: The figure draws only three query-head groups followed by an ellipsis, while the label says '× 8 groups'. A reader can momentarily read the drawing as three groups total rather than a schematic excerpt of eight.
evidence: The figure shows three groups of eight query heads, each connected to one K/V head, then '…'. The label below says '8 query heads : 1 K/V head (× 8 groups)'.

figure: Figure 7.2 — Hybrid history: two state lifetimes
issue: The top row draws three fixed-size state boxes side by side, which can visually suggest three retained states even though the caption says recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained. The corrective text is present but the layout still carries the wrong first impression.
evidence: The figure shows 'state after t1', 'state after t2', and 'state after t3' as three separate boxes in parallel columns. The caption says 'recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained.'
acceptance_test: Redraw the top row so succession is visually dominant—e.g. a single state box updated in place across t1→t2→t3, or a timeline with explicit 'overwrite' arrows—so a reader cannot infer joint retention from the layout alone.

figure: Figure 7.3 — Quantization choices and execution paths
issue: The execution-path branch is labeled 'Native FP4 math', but the numerical-representation box includes INT4. The figure does not show a native-INT4 path, so a reader may infer that INT4 executes through FP4 math or that the branch applies to all listed formats.
evidence: Top-right box: 'INT4 + scheme / MXFP4 / NVFP4'. Bottom-left branch: 'Native FP4 math / Compatible low-bit operand arithmetic'. The caption says only supported combinations can load and execute.

figure: Figure 7.6 — Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning
issue: The 2×H100 (160 GB) reference line crosses the inference bar near its top, and the bar's hatching can obscure the dashed line at print size. The inference bar is only ~5 GB above the line, so the visual relationship is easy to misread.

issue: The vertical resource ladder places execution units (tensor cores/ALU) between registers and shared memory and runs the 'capacity grows' gradient through them, conflating compute throughput with memory capacity.
evidence: The box 'tensor cores / ALU — arithmetic units' sits under the red 'capacity grows speed drops distance grows' arrow; the caption calls the ladder a resource hierarchy but does not say tensor cores are compute-only.

issue: The text 'GPU↔GPU and host link' in the green interconnect box is set tight against the left border and may clip or touch the border at print size.

issue: The caption says 'only ~1–2 at 128K', but the figure's own KV 335 GB and the fixed 436 GB KV budget imply 436/335 ≈ 1.30, i.e., one full request, not two.

issue: The green blocks are not explained as the first decode step of a backfilled sequence; because they are followed by blue blocks, a reader can plausibly infer that green is a separate short sequence that ends and is replaced by another blue sequence.

acceptance_test: Add a note or label stating that green marks the first decode step of a backfilled sequence and that the following blue is the same sequence continuing; or redraw so the entire backfilled sequence is visually identified.

issue: The annotation 'a finishing sequence frees its slot immediately' points at a green block, which is the new sequence, not the finishing sequence or the freed slot. The arrow therefore points to the wrong object.
evidence: Rendered figure: the arrow from that text terminates on a green block. The green block is the backfill sequence; the finishing sequence is the preceding blue block.
acceptance_test: Move the arrow to the boundary between the finishing blue block and the green backfill block, or relabel the annotation to 'a freed slot is refilled immediately'.

issue: The 'next batch waits' annotation is a gray box with an arrow pointing to a row, not to the batch-completion boundary. It is visually ambiguous whether the next batch waits for that row, for the whole batch, or for the end of the time axis.

issue: Blue and green are both solid fills and are distinguished only by color; the caption also uses color names ('green', 'pink') as load-bearing descriptors. In grayscale the blue/green distinction is not reliably recoverable.

figure: Figure 15.1 — FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic
issue: In the BEFORE panel, the red annotation reads "O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block". The colon attributes the O(L²) traffic to K/V row-block re-reads — but K/V row-block reads from HBM are O(L²) in BOTH the naive and FlashAttention implementations (each query tile still needs all K/V). The quantity that actually drops is the materialized L×L intermediate, which the AFTER panel mentions only as "no L×L intermediate at HBM" with no complexity label. Juxtaposing an "O(L²)" label on the left against no complexity label on the right invites the reader to infer that FlashAttention changes the asymptotic HBM-traffic class — precisely the "quadratic-to-linear swap" misconception that the book's own prose on PDF 247 explicitly warns against ("the precise I/O complexity is more nuanced than a clean quadratic-to-linear swap").
evidence: Fig 15.1 BEFORE panel: "O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block". AFTER panel: "K/V reused per tile — no single global K/V pass; no L×L intermediate at HBM" (no big-O label). Prose on PDF 247 / printed 227: "the precise I/O complexity is more nuanced than a clean quadratic-to-linear swap, but the materialized-intermediate traffic is what drops". acceptance_test: Table 17-1 states the token count behind 24.9037 GB; that token count matches the canonical whole-context stated in Ch. 4 / Table 4-2; and re-deriving C and N_min from the stated context reproduces 17 slots and 21 hosts.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge
issue: The caption's stated prefill arithmetic intensity (~41 FLOP/byte) contradicts BOTH the plotted marker (~10^4 FLOP/byte) and the prose on the same page (~2K FLOP/byte). Three mutually inconsistent values are given for the single quantity the figure exists to convey. Worse, the caption's own number (41) is BELOW the ridge the figure labels (~295), so taken at face value the caption places prefill on the memory-bound side while simultaneously calling it 'the compute-bound side'.
evidence: Caption (printed p.23): 'Low-batch decode (streaming weights per token) lands at ~1 FLOP/byte — the memory-bound side; long-prefix prefill lands at ~41 FLOP/byte — the compute-bound side.' Prose list item (1) on the same page: 'arithmetic intensity places the canonical prefill point ~2K FLOP/byte, well to the right of the ~295 ridge'. Figure: the blue 'prefill' triangle sits at the far right of the x-axis, at or beyond the 10000 tick (AI ~ 1e4), not at 41 and not at 2e3. Independent rederivation for the canonical 70B / 9,200-token prefill: FLOPs = 2 x 70e9 x 9200 = 1.29e15; bytes = 140 GB weights + 2.62 MB/token x 9200 = 24.1 GB KV writes = 1.64e11 B; AI = 1.29e15 / 1.64e11 ~ 7.8e3 FLOP/byte (plus ~17% from attention FLOPs -> ~9e3). None of 41, 2e3, or 1e4 is derivable from the canonical numbers as printed; 41 is also implausible on its face, since prefill AI is approximately the number of tokens processed (AI ~ T for large T), so 'long-prefix prefill' cannot be 41.
root_cause: The figure, its caption, and the summary list were authored from three different (unstated) derivations of the same quantity; no single derivation is shown anywhere on the page, so no gate could catch the divergence.
correction: Pick one canonical prefill AI, show its derivation (tokens, FLOPs, bytes, ratio) in the caption or in an adjacent worked example, and make the caption, the marker position, and the prose list item all state that same value. If the intended value is the derived ~8e3, move the marker to ~8e3 and rewrite the caption as '~8x10^3 FLOP/byte — the compute-bound side'. If a different scenario (e.g. a short prompt) is intended, label it as such and plot a second marker rather than silently changing the number.
acceptance_test: One number appears for canonical prefill AI in the caption, in the marker x-position, and in prose item (1); the value exceeds 295 (so 'compute-bound side' is true of the stated number); and a reader can reproduce it from the canonical inputs printed in Ch. 4 / Table 2-1 without consulting another chapter.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge
issue: The drawn roofline ridge is geometrically inconsistent with its own '~295' crossover label and with the H100 numbers the book uses elsewhere, and the decode marker is drawn ON the ridge, contradicting the figure's own annotation that markers lie below the roof.
evidence: A roofline's bandwidth-limited segment is a straight line in log-log with slope = HBM bandwidth and NO intercept; it must pass through (AI=1, performance = bandwidth). For H100 SXM (FP16 dense 989 TFLOPS, HBM3 3.35 TB/s) the ridge is performance = 3.35e12 x AI, i.e. it crosses the 989 TFLOPS peak at AI = 295 and passes through (1, 3.35e12). The drawn line instead intercepts the y-axis at ~1e12 at AI = 1 and reaches 1e15 at AI ~ 295; those two constraints cannot be satisfied by one straight line (the drawn line implies a bandwidth of ~1.6 TB/s and a crossover at ~600, or, if the drawn slope is 1 decade/decade, a bandwidth of 1 TB/s and a crossover at 1000). The red 'decode' circle at (1, ~1.2e12) is drawn directly on the black ridge line, while the in-figure annotation states 'markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)'. The decode marker should sit clearly BELOW the ridge (roofline at AI=1 is 3.35e12; decode at batch 1 achieves ~3.35e12 only in the idealized bandwidth-bound limit, and real kernels sit below it).
root_cause: The ridge was drawn by eye against the axis limits rather than computed from the peak/bandwidth pair, so the intercept, the crossover label, and the marker placement were never reconciled.
correction: Redraw the ridge from the actual numbers: bandwidth-limited segment through (1, 3.35e12) and (295, 9.89e14), with the compute-bound plateau at 9.89e14 (label it 989 TFLOPS, not 1e15). Place the decode marker at (1, ~1e12) clearly below the ridge, and the prefill marker at its derived AI and at a plausible sub-peak performance (e.g. 3-5e14). If the intent was to show decode sitting exactly on the bandwidth roofline, say so in the caption and remove the 'run below the roof' annotation.
acceptance_test: The drawn ridge satisfies performance = 3.35e12 x AI for AI <= 295 and performance = 9.89e14 for AI >= 295; the '~295' label coincides with the drawn crossover; no marker lies on the ridge line unless the caption explicitly says it is on the roofline; the y-axis plateau is labelled 989 TFLOPS.

Alternatively, if the intent is that the first token enters the loop at the point where 'next token' is produced, redraw the loop so the sampled token is visibly re-injected at 'previous token' and drop the separate initialize arrow.
acceptance_test: Tracing only the arrows (ignoring the caption), a reader concludes that the first sampled token becomes the input of the first decode step, and no arrow terminates on the 'next token' box from outside the loop.

figure: FIGURE 2.1 — The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline

Adopt one book-wide palette in which, e.g., KV state is always purple, cache writes always one hue and cache reads always another, and request/control flow always a third; then add the 'color is figure-local' disclaimer to every figure caption that uses color, or drop the disclaimer and make the palette global.

figure: FIGURE 2.1 — The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline
issue: The PREFILL band shows a single 'token + position' box for a pass the caption calls 'the one-shot parallel pass over the whole prompt', inviting the reading that prefill processes one token at a time — the exact misconception the prefill/decode distinction exists to prevent.
evidence: PREFILL band: 'prompt -> token + position -> transformer -> logits + sampling -> first token' (one box). DECODE band: 'previous token -> token + position -> transformer -> logits + sampling -> next token' (one box, correctly, since decode is one token per step). Caption: 'PREFILL (top) is the one-shot parallel pass over the whole prompt.' The two bands are visually identical in token granularity, so the parallelism of prefill is carried only by prose.

acceptance_test: A reader who sees only the figure (no caption) can state that prefill processes all prompt tokens in one parallel pass while decode processes one token per step.

figure: FIGURE 2.1 — The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline
issue: Layout inconsistencies: the italic note 'conceptual per-step, per-layer cache I/O' sits inside the DECODE band against its top border; the band labels are placed inconsistently ('PREFILL' above its band, 'DECODE' inside its band); the 'read' and 'append' arrows are only ~0.35 in apart with their labels offset to opposite sides, which is tight for a figure whose whole point is the read/write distinction.

issue: The figure depicts each token's K/V being appended on the SAME step the token is sampled, contradicting the figure's own caption and the book's prose. This is the single most consequential semantic detail in the chapter (it is what makes the KV cache a cache rather than a recomputation), and the drawing gets it backwards.
evidence: Caption: 'every token adds one K/V per layer per head — written when that token is next processed as an input, one step after it is sampled.' Drawing: token1 ('sampled from prefill'), token2 ('first decode output'), token3 ('second decode output') each have a direct arrow into the 'append K/V per layer-head' box, i.e. the sampled token's own K/V is appended at the step it is sampled. Prose on printed p.14 (PDF p.34) states the opposite explicitly: 'the sampled next token is the output of this step and the input of the following step, whose forward pass then computes and appends its K/V. A token's K/V therefore enters the cache on the step in which it is the input, not on the step in which it is sampled.'
root_cause: The figure was drawn as a token-to-cache accumulation story rather than as a step-indexed story, so the one-step lag that the caption and prose emphasize is not encoded.
correction: Re-index the figure by step: show 'step t: input token_{i-1} -> compute K/V -> append K/V for token_{i-1}' and 'step t+1: input token_i -> ...', with the sampled token_i shown as the OUTPUT of step t and the INPUT of step t+1. At minimum, add a one-step offset between the token column and the append box (e.g. a bracket labelled 'appended on the NEXT step') and change the token sub-labels to 'sampled at step t' / 'appended at step t+1'.
acceptance_test: Tracing only the arrows, a reader concludes that a token's K/V is written on the step in which that token is the input, not on the step in which it is sampled; the figure and the printed p.14 prose agree without needing the caption to arbitrate.

issue: An unlabeled connector runs from the top of the token column across the top of the figure and drops into the top of the 'append K/V per layer-head' box. Its origin and meaning are not stated anywhere, and it duplicates the side connector from the same token column into the same box, so the reader cannot tell whether it is a feedback path, a second input, or a stray artifact.

The token column boxes sit at x~95-165 with their tops at y~185, so the line appears to originate just above token1. correction: Either delete the top connector, or give it a definite meaning and label it. If it is meant to express the loop (cache read -> next token -> next step), route it from the 'read for attention' box back to the token column and label it 'next step's input', which would also make the one-step lag of FIG-1.1-A visible.
acceptance_test: Every connector in the figure has a label or an unambiguous source and destination; no two connectors connect the same pair of elements with different implied meanings.

figure: FIGURE 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior

Red label above the grid: 'top-2 active'. Legend line beneath: 'active experts = 2 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'. Caption: 'the two routed experts (~11.4B + ~5.7B)'. evidence: Rendered legend line: 'active experts = 2 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'. 2 × 11.4 = 22.8 GB. Caption: '~22.8 GB is active per token' and '~94 GB' resident. Cross-check: 68 GB (inactive) + 22.8 GB (active) + 2.8 GB (shared 1.4B) = 93.6 GB ≈ 94 GB, which only closes with 22.8, not 2.

figure: FIGURE 3.4 — KV comparison boxes ('dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB')
issue: The KV comparison is not reproducible from the shape labels printed beside it. issue: This caption is set in italic and appears centred, while every other caption in the batch is roman and justified. A single figure breaking the caption convention reads as a production accident.
evidence: Printed p.91: 'FIGURE 6.1: The metric hierarchy as a diagnostic chain [ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]. issue: The note enumerating the full-fine-tune memory components does not sum to the plotted bar value of ~1,120 GB. issue: The shaded 'SLO-violating' region does not begin at the SLO line. figure: FIGURE 7.7 — Concurrency budget — one 8×H100 host (640 GB pool)
issue: The displayed substitution line under the figure reads "≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests". The operator between the two quantities is a plus sign, but the arithmetic requires division (436 ÷ 24.9 = 17.51). As printed, the equation is false: 436 + 24.9 = 460.9, not 17.5. It also contradicts the line immediately above it, which correctly states "in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request".
evidence: Rendered page 145, display block between the bar and the caption: line 1 "in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request"; line 2 "≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests". Caption confirms the intended operation: "at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C = 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18…)". 436 ÷ 24.9 = 17.51 ✓; 436 + 24.9 = 460.9 ✗. The same figure's caption also uses the correct division for the FP8 case (436 ÷ 12.45 ≈ 35).
acceptance_test: Open the source for the FIGURE 7.7 display and confirm the operator glyph is '÷' (or ' / '), not '+'. If the source is correct, re-render at 300 dpi and confirm the glyph is a division sign on the page; if the source is wrong, change '+' to '÷' and re-check that the display still reads "≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests". Also confirm no downstream text quotes the '+' form.

issue: The caption sentence is grammatically broken and logically ambiguous: "and that KV budget is the per-request KV price sets concurrency". The intended relation (budget ÷ per-request price = concurrency) is not stated; as written the sentence has no main verb and could be read as claiming the budget *is* the price.
evidence: Rendered page 145, caption line 2–3: "…host's 640 GB pool, and that KV budget is the per-request KV price sets concurrency — at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C = 17.5 concurrent…". The figure's own display (line 1) states the correct relation, so the caption is the only place the relation is stated in words.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as: "…and that KV budget, divided by the per-request KV price, sets concurrency — at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C = 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18…)". Confirm the rewritten sentence names both operands and the operation.

acceptance_test: Move "640 GB pool" immediately after the title text (or into the title itself: "Concurrency budget — one 8×H100 host, 640 GB pool"), and add a one-line note such as "bar width ∝ GB" to the figure or caption. Confirm the drawn segment widths are proportional to 140 : 64 : 436 within a few percent.

issue: The caption makes a specific, load-bearing claim about a graphic feature — "the faint vertical rules inside the KV band are those 24.9 GB request slots" — but the rules are drawn at very low contrast. figure: FIGURE 7.8 — Memory Tetris (scale note vs. drawing)
issue: The figure's own note says "Bar heights are not to scale (GB)", yet the drawing is (or appears to be) to scale: the light horizontal rules are spaced at 80 GB intervals across the 640 GB pool, and the three bar tops land at roughly 36% / 45% / 84% of the 640 GB dashed line, i.e. 229 / 288 / 539 GB. One of the two statements is false. If the note is true, then the "640 GB = 8× 80 GB ranks" dashed line and the "light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries" are meaningless decoration and the reader will misread the 128K bar as nearly filling the host. If the note is false, the note is a factual error in the figure.
evidence: Rendered page 146: note under the bars reads "The baseline (weights + runtime) is fixed; only the KV cache grows with context. Bar heights are not to scale (GB)." Against that: the red dashed 640 GB line sits above all three bars; the light rules are evenly spaced at ~1/8 of the plot height (consistent with 80 GB × 8); bar tops are at ≈229/288/539 GB, which are exactly the values printed under the bars ("= 229 GB used", "= 288 GB used", "= 539 GB used").

issue: The rules are labelled "light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries", but they are drawn as horizontal lines across the plot. A rank boundary is a division between GPUs (8 GPUs side by side), which can only be represented by vertical partitions; horizontal lines at 80 GB intervals are capacity gridlines, not rank boundaries. The caption repeats the mislabel ("the 80 GB rank-boundary lines are a visualization guide").
evidence: Rendered page 146: subtitle "(light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries)" above a set of horizontal light rules; caption: "…the 80 GB rank-boundary lines are a visualization guide; sharding, KV partitioning, interconnect must be validated per rank." No vertical partition of the 640 GB pool into 8 × 80 GB is drawn anywhere.
acceptance_test: Rename the rules to "80 GB capacity gridlines" in both the figure subtitle and the caption, or draw eight vertical partitions labelled R0…R7 to show the actual rank boundaries. Confirm the caption's caveat about per-rank validation still reads correctly against whichever treatment is chosen.

issue: The concurrency consequence is stated only for two of the three bars, and the 128K figure is loose: "only ~1–2 at 128K". 436 / 335 = 1.30, i.e. one concurrent request (floor), not "~1–2". evidence: Rendered page 146 caption: "…consuming the fixed ~436 GB KV budget (17.5 concurrent at 9.5K, floor 17; only ~1–2 at 128K)". Figure labels: KV 24.9 GB (9.5K), KV 84 GB (32K), KV 335 GB (128K). 436/24.9 = 17.5 ✓; 436/84 = 5.19; 436/335 = 1.30.

evidence: Rendered page 152: seven stacked boxes, four blue, one orange, two green; no legend. issue: The red vertical arrow carries the figure's central gradient message but is ambiguous in two ways: it has a single arrowhead at the top (pointing toward "small · fast · close") while the adjacent red text describes the downward direction ("capacity grows / speed drops / distance grows"), and it spans only the middle portion of the stack (roughly L2 down to "other GPUs / remote") rather than the full ladder from registers to remote GPUs.

issue: The ladder is presented as a "speed↔capacity↔distance" ranking, but the ordering of HBM above GPU interconnect is a latency/distance statement, not a bandwidth statement: HBM bandwidth (3.35 TB/s on H100) is roughly 7× NVLink bandwidth (~450 GB/s). A reader who takes the ladder as a bandwidth ordering will mispredict which resource binds first in TP.
evidence: Rendered page 152 caption: "The gradient of speed↔capacity↔distance is why compute, memory bandwidth, memory capacity and interconnect bandwidth are distinct architectural constraints…" The figure places "GPU interconnect" below "HBM (GPU memory)" on a single monotone ladder.

issue: The caption states "the peak roofline is 989 TFLOPS (H100) / 1,979 TFLOPS (H200)". evidence: Rendered page 159 caption: "Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs, so the peak roofline is 989 TFLOPS (H100) / 1,979 TFLOPS (H200)." Figure: one shared plateau annotated "compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS"; ridge labels "ridge = 295" (H100) and "ridge = 206" (H200). Check: 989/3.35 = 295 ✓ and 989/4.8 = 206 ✓; 1,979/4.8 = 412 ✗ (matches no label in the figure).
acceptance_test: Correct the caption to "the peak roofline is 989 TFLOPS dense FP16 for both H100 and H200 (1,979 TFLOPS is the sparsity figure, and the FP8 dense figure)", and confirm the figure's plateau annotation and both ridge labels remain consistent with 989 TFLOPS. Add a regression check that no H200 dense-FP16 peak of 1,979 appears anywhere in the book.

issue: The caption contains a direct self-contradiction about the same operating point: "decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the compute-bound side; decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope". Decode at batch=1 cannot be on both sides. The correct statement (per the facing page) is that decode at batch=1 sits at ≈1 FLOP/byte, far left, on the memory-bound slope, and that batching moves it rightward up that slope. Two further clauses are garbled: "the ridge point is the memory-bound slope (per-GPU)" (the ridge is where the memory-bound slope meets the compute-bound plateau) and "host-level attainable performance adds additional depends on scheduling and communication".
evidence: Rendered page 159 caption, sentences 3–5: "…Prefill (9.2K input) sits to the right of the compute-bound ridge (batch=1) — it is not a measured latency; decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the compute-bound side; decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope and continues batching climbs the slope as batch grows." Facing page (printed 140): "decode intensity ≈ 1 FLOP/byte at batch=1 and ≈ 32 FLOP/byte at batch=32".
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption so each operating point is described exactly once and consistently: prefill (9.2K) right of the ridge; decode batch=1 left of the ridge on the memory-bound slope; decode batched climbing that slope toward the ridge. Replace "the ridge point is the memory-bound slope" with "the ridge point is where the memory-bound slope meets the compute-bound plateau", and fix "adds additional depends on" to "additionally depends on". The 32K value (4.59 PFLOP) and the canonical 9.2K value (1.29 PFLOP) are both correct under 2·70B·L, so the '1K' figure is the sole outlier and is 2x too high. If a prefix of P tokens is shared by r requests and each request also carries an uncached suffix S, per-request prefill falls from (S + P) to (S + P/r), so the ratio f(r) = (S + P/r)/(S + P) is convex-decreasing: the largest saving occurs between r = 1 and r = 10 and the curve then flattens toward S/(S + P).

The figure therefore teaches 'prefix caching's per-request saving accelerates with reuse', which is a false model of the mechanism and would mislead a reader sizing prefill headroom.

The correct expression is N* = N_params/(n_layers x d) = 70e9/(80 x 8,192) = 106,811 ~ 106.8K (and 53.4K for the full-square convention, N_params/(2 x n_layers x d)). In grayscale the two palettes overlap: the medium-blue band 'Inside agent runtime' and the medium-green band 'Inside attention' render at similar mid-grays, and the light-blue 'Inside tools' / light-green 'Inside weights' likewise. A print reader cannot map the legend's color words to the bands, so the system-vs-model split (the figure's main message) is lost. No non-color cue (border style, hatching, divider, or bracket) separates the two groups.
evidence: Legend line: 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs'. Bands 2–5 use a blue gradient, bands 6–8 a green gradient; all share the same solid-border style, so hue is the only group discriminator. acceptance_test: Add a non-color cue separating the system group (top 5 bands) from the model group (bottom 3 bands) — e.g. a horizontal divider line with a small 'SYSTEM' / 'MODEL' bracket label on the left, or distinct border styles/hatching per group — and re-verify in a grayscale render that a reader can identify which bands are 'system' vs 'model' without using the color words in the legend.

evidence: Rendered 'Actual stop' row: pass 1 → pass 2, then a solid line/arrow into the dashed 'pass 3' box (captioned 'not executed'), then a solid arrow to the tan 'exit' box. issue: The ④ OUTCOME box headline reads 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a)·(b)', which presents candidates (a) and (b) as having passed the capacity/throughput gate. This contradicts the figure's own caption ('three conditional candidates, each with its own open validation gate (not a settled verdict) ... no candidate is deployment-validated') and Table 12-1 on PDF 222 / printed 202, where row (b) verdict is 'conditional finalist — ✗ throughput at a single prefill host (~19.8K ≪ ~92K); prefill pool must itself scale to ~5 hosts'. evidence: Figure box text: 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a)·(b) / each needs ~5 hosts of prefill capacity'. Table 12-1 row (b) verdict column: 'conditional finalist — ✗ throughput at a single prefill host (~19.8K ≪ ~92K); prefill pool must itself scale to ~5 hosts (92K ÷ 19.8K ≈ 4.65)'.
acceptance_test: Reword the OUTCOME box so the figure matches the caption's 'open validation gate' and the table's 'conditional finalist', e.g. 'CONDITIONAL on capacity gate (a)·(b) — each needs ~5 prefill hosts (to be measured at target load)'. After the edit, a reader who looks only at the figure (not the caption) must not be able to conclude that (a) or (b) is deployment-validated to meet the SLO.

issue: The x-axis quantity 'Avg prefix reuse' is used as the independent variable of the left plot but is never defined in the caption or the surrounding prose. issue: Wording tension between caption and in-plot annotation. issue: The in-figure title uses the British spelling 'specialised' ('Routing every request to the right specialised model (sequential cascade)'), which may conflict with the US '-ize' house style used in body text. issue: The left panel's x-axis ends at 10^2 K (100K), but the in-plot annotation 'causal-triangle: crossover ~106.8K' refers to a point off-scale (106.8K > 100K). The green leader line points to the green dotted 'total (causal-triangle)' curve, which equals linear + causal-quad and is therefore strictly greater than the red 'linear 2·N·L' curve for all L — it never crosses it. The causal-quad curve itself is not drawn, so the figure does not actually depict the 106.8K crossover and the leader mislabels the total curve as the crossover.
evidence: x-axis ticks are 10^0, 10^1, 10^2 (K tokens); legend: green dotted = 'total (causal-triangle)', purple dash-dot = 'quadratic 4·n_layers·L^2·d' (full-square only). Causal-quad = 0.5·full-quad is not plotted. Note 22.1-1 (p. 340) gives the causal crossover as L* = N/(n_layers·d) ≈ 106.8K, which exceeds the 100K axis limit.
acceptance_test: Either extend the left panel x-axis to ≥ 1.1×10^2 K and draw the causal-quad curve (or add a vertical guide at 106.8K) so the crossover is visible, or remove the in-plot 'causal-triangle: crossover ~106.8K' leader and keep that value only in the caption/note; in no case may a leader point to the green dotted total curve as if it were the crossover.

issue: Box 1 states the problem as 'TTFT p95 2.1 s' but Box 2 states the success criterion as 'p5 TTFT ≤ 2 s'. A p5 (low-percentile) target of 2 s is already met by any system whose p95 is 2.1 s, so the success gate does not address the stated tail-latency problem and contradicts the chapter's p95-SLO framing (e.g., §21.8, where p95 TTFT drifting past the SLO is the failure mode). This is almost certainly a p95→p5 typo that breaks the funnel's internal logic.
evidence: Box 1 line: '"our app is slow" → TTFT p95 2.1 s on a 70B model'. Box 2 line: 'p5 TTFT ≤ 2 s, ~25 ms/token, 40 rps peak'.
acceptance_test: Change Box 2 to 'p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s' (or align both boxes to the same percentile) so the success gate tightens the tail metric named in the problem box.
